transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-10-29
- Start: 14:30 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Recording: yes
- Notes: security-focused review, two Redwood AE/SE + Security PM, Lucent InfoSec/CTO/Legal/Infra

Summary:
Quick security and privacy review focused on data residency, KMS/BYOK, audit log retention, RBAC/SSO, and our 'no training on customer data' assurances. Lucent asked for specific retention windows for prompts and logs, proof points (SOC2/ISO), and options for private deployment vs hosted with EU residency.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2/ISO artifacts and timeline
- SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC mapping
- Audit logs: retention and export for Lucent SIEM
- Encryption: at rest/in transit, BYOK via AWS KMS or HSM options
- Data residency: routing to EU region, Dedicated/Private deployments
- Prompt/content retention and 'no training' guarantee; PII/PHI handling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for making time, appreciate it. we'll keep this tightly scoped to your security questions — Maya's our SE who'll take the infra bits.
[00:25] Priya (Lucent): Thanks Samir, Priya here. we want to understand how you handle prompts containing PII/PHI and what guarantees you provide that data won't be used to train models. also curious about EU residency and keys.
[00:40] Maya (Redwood): Totally. high-level: hosted API by default stores minimal prompt logs for troubleshooting and billing, retention configurable. Redwood's policy is customer data is not used to train models by default — we have an explicit no-train contract addendum for enterprise customers.
[01:05] Lena (Lucent): When you say "not used to train" is that contractual or a config toggle? we need something we can point to in a DPA.
[01:15] Jordan (Redwood): It's both. we have the platform-level defaults, and for enterprise we sign the no-training clause in the contract. operationally we also support ephemerality settings so prompts are not persisted beyond X days — or can be set to ephemeral-only where they are discarded immediately after response.
[01:40] Marco (Lucent): ephemeral-only sounds good, but we'll need logs for audits. what's the tradeoff?
[01:48] Maya (Redwood): right, ephemeral-only removes stored prompt content; however, you lose long-term traces. we can haved a hybrid: keep metadata and hashes for audit, but redact content, or keep full audit logs in a customer-managed S3 bucket for a fixed retention period.
[02:10] Ethan (Lucent): for our regulator we need audit logs available 365 days and data resident in the EU. can you guarantee that?
[02:18] Samir (Redwood): Yes — we have EU regions. Hosted API traffic can be routed and served from EU data centers. additionally Dedicated and Private deployments give you full tenancy and VPC controls. we can set log retention to 365 days and either ship logs to your SIEM or give you direct S3 access.
[02:35] Priya: and encryption — we require customer-managed keys (BYOK). does Redwood support that?
[02:42] Jordan: Yes. BYOK via AWS KMS is supported in Hosted with Private KMS integration for enterprise tenants, and in Dedicated/Private you can use your own HSM/KMS. All tokens are encrypted at rest and in transit. we also do envelope encryption for model caches and persisted KV cache snapshots.
[03:05] Lena: what about auditability for key usage — we need key rotation logs and evidence that keys were only used for Lucent workloads.
[03:13] Maya: if you onboard to Dedicated we can ensure KMS keys are in your account or in a customer-controlled account. for Hosted with BYOK we provide key usage logs and can share KMS access logs on request; we'll add that to the SOC2 artifact pack.
[03:30] Priya: SOC2 — do you have Type II? and ISO?
[03:36] Samir: we completed SOC2 Type II in 2026 and maintain ISO27001 scope across our cloud control plane; I will share the reports.
[03:45] Marco: is there an option for an on-prem or air-gapped package?
[03:50] Jordan: Yes — Redwood Private is designed for air-gapped or on-prem installs. it's a customer-managed control plane with an installer and optional support. we can exclude outbound telemetry entirely in that mode.
[04:05] Ethan: regarding the 'no training' claim, how do we prove it operationally? are there logs to show model retraining jobs don't include our prompts?
[04:14] Maya: good question — we provide a combination of contractual guarantees, internal process docs, and audit evidence. we maintain separate datasets for public experiments versus customer data. retraining pipelines are isolated and we can provide attestations for discrete windows. for enterprise customers we can also arrange a scoped audit.
[04:40] Priya: okay. can you detail prompt retention defaults and what the UI/ API controls are?
[04:47] Jordan: default is 30 days for prompt retention in hosted mode. you can change that via policy to 0 days (ephemeral), 7, 30, 90, or set a custom TTL. policies can be applied per-project, per-route, or token-level.
[05:05] Priya: if we set 0 days, does that also remove the ability to debug production issues?
[05:12] Maya: it removes stored text but we can keep non-sensitive metadata: request ID, timestamp, model used, latency, token counts. for deeper debugging we offer a temporary retention window — e.g., ephemeral + 72-hour debug logs accessible only to your security group, and auto-deleted thereafter.
[05:34] Lena: is there redaction at ingress? auto-PHI/PII detection to scrub content?
[05:39] Jordan: we have an optional pre-processing hook: you can run an on-premisered PII scrubber or use Redwood's built-in detectors. the built-in detectors do regex and ML-based PII detection and can redact or hash detected items before persisting. we don't rely on that for contractual obligations — it's an optional layer.
[06:05] Priya: retention of embeddings — do embeddings count as training data? if we store vector embeddings in the platform, could those leak content?
[06:14] Maya: embeddings are treated as derived data; they can be persisted per your policy. they aren't used to train shared model weights. still, embeddings can leak information in theory, so for regulated workloads we recommend ephemeral embeddings or store them in your VPC-backed Dedicated instance where you control storage.
[06:35] Marco: log export — we need real-time streaming to our SIEM, and guaranteed delivery.
[06:41] Samir: we support log streaming via Kinesis/EventBridge or direct HTTPS forwarder to your SIEM. Guaranteed delivery is configurable with retries and dead-letter queues; alternatively we can drop logs in an S3 bucket in your account.
[06:58] Ethan: SSO — SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping?
[07:04] Jordan: we support SAML SSO for user auth and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with pre-defined roles and custom roles. you can map SAML assertions to roles and we support fine-grained route-level permissions.
[07:25] Priya: retention of admin actions and audit trails — for compliance we need immutable logs for admin actions.
[07:32] Maya: admin audits are captured separately and can be set to immutable retention policies. we can forward to your WORM S3 or SIEM.
[07:42] Lena: data residency for model inference — are all inference computations guaranteed to run within the EU if we elect EU region? any potential fallback to other regions?
[07:52] Samir: policy-driven routing allows you to pin inference to EU regions. fallbacks only happen if you opt into cross-region failover; otherwise we will queue or reject traffic when capacity is exceeded. for Dedicated/Private you get stronger locality guarantees.
[08:12] Marco: about model variants — if a smaller quantized model is used for cost, does that change privacy or training posture?
[08:19] Maya: model variant doesn't change the training posture — that is orthogonal. but we do maintain model variant catalogs and will document which variant served each request in the audit logs.
[08:32] Ethan: any certifications around penetration testing?
[08:35] Jordan: yearly third-party pentest; we provide summary reports and remediation timelines. detailed pentest reports are available under NDA.
[08:46] Priya: want to confirm deletion semantics: if we delete a project, are all prompts and embeddings purged from backups and KV caches?
[08:55] Maya: deletion triggers immediate deletion from active stores; backups are tombstoned and purged within the next backup cycle (max 30 days). for stricter needs we offer on-demand purge and certificate of deletion for enterprise accounts.
[09:12] Lena: can you sign a clause that you won't use our content to improve models and will delete any cached KV snapshots on request?
[09:19] Samir: yes, contractually we can commit to "no training" and to purge KV caches upon request; we'll include the language in the addendum.
[09:28] Marco: network egress — does Redwood make outbound connections that might route data via third-party analytics?
[09:34] Jordan: by default telemetry is collected for performance and SLA monitoring, but for enterprise/private you can disable telemetry or route it to your collectors only. we don't route prompt contents to third-party analytics.
[09:48] Ethan: multi-tenant in hosted — how do you separate keys/stores across tenants?
[09:54] Maya: tenant isolation is via namespaces, per-tenant KMS keys, and per-tenant storage buckets. secrets are scoped per-tenant and role.
[10:06] Priya: about model training pipelines — what process prevents accidental inclusion of customer data?
[10:12] Jordan: policy: customer data is labeled and access-controlled. training pipelines pull only curated corpora from internal datasets. we also have gating reviews and a separation of duties. we can provide attestation artifacts for auditors.
[10:27] Samir: i'll note we have an internal change freeze window for model training that is tracked, and for any enterprise dataset we maintain an inclusion log.
[10:36] Priya: can Redwood support a short compliance walkthrough with our auditors?
[10:40] Samir: yes, we do customer audits and can schedule a 60-minute session; we'll prepare the artifact pack (SOC2, ISO, pentest summary, KMS procedures).
[10:51] Lena: regarding DPA and SCCs — any known limitations with the wording?
[10:55] Jordan: standard language; we usually accept SCCs and have an enterprise DPA which includes security controls. we'll share the template.
[11:05] Marco: performance/latency: if we pin to EU models, are there cost increases?
[11:11] Maya: slight cost delta for region egress and capacity reserved; we can provide an estimate once we know throughput. Dedicated gives more predictable unit economics.
[11:25] Ethan: can we get a short POC where we send sample prompts (with redacted PHI) and confirm logs and keys are captured correctly?
[11:31] Samir: yes, we can do a scoped POC in your EU provisioned environment. Maya will run benchmarks and also validate KMS/BYOK flow.
[11:40] Priya: log format: need RFC3339 timestamps, request ids, model version and route.
[11:45] Jordan: that's standard; we'll provide JSON schema for logs.
[11:50] Lena: what about legal hold — if our legal team needs to preserve certain prompts for e-discovery can you honor that?
[11:56] Maya: yes, legal hold is supported for enterprise accounts. it prevents automatic deletion until the hold is released.
[12:05] Samir: circling back, we'll share the SOC2 and ISO artifacts and the DPA/SCC template. we'll also propose a 2-week POC schedule.
[12:16] Priya: sounds good. will you also share the ephemeral retention config docs and the API for setting TTLs?
[12:21] Maya: yes, will include API snippets and a sample policy.
[12:28] Lena: last question, how do you handle subpoenas or legal requests for customer content?
[12:33] Jordan: we notify customers as soon as legally allowed and have a lawful access process. in Private deployments you control the keys so Redwood can't decrypt customer data without your cooperation.
[12:50] [wrap-up] Samir: cool — next steps we summarized earlier. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
